title: Durably record attempt release disposition with lease and provider-slot state
description:
Objective: produce the release facts `ExpansionReleaseEvidence` requires and nothing in production currently writes. Producer repair for task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4, whose rail 1 states: "if it omits a named fact, repair that producer rather than reconstructing authority here."

MEASURED GAP at HEAD fa39721, field by field across apps/daemon/src (non-test). `ExpansionReleaseEvidence` (packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-planning-hold.ts:27-36) declares 17 fields. These six have NO production producer — every occurrence in apps/daemon is inside a `*-test-fixtures.ts` file:
- `reason` and `disposition{resumable, strongestReason, terminalTarget}` — `strongestReason` and `terminalTarget` appear once each, both in apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-test-fixtures.ts:107-108.
- `attemptState` — twice, both recovery-test-fixtures.ts:123,142.
- `leaseRef` — once, apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:191. `leaseState` — ZERO.
- `providerSlotRef` — once, bootstrap-test-fixtures.ts:192. `providerSlotState` — ZERO.
- `WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE` — ZERO hits anywhere in apps/daemon.

That last one is load-bearing: core's acceptance predicate (expansion-planning-hold.ts:210-213) admits release evidence only when `truthClass === "DAEMON_VERIFIED"` AND `reason === "WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE"` AND `disposition.strongestReason === "WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE"` AND `disposition.terminalTarget === "RELEASED"`. The vocabulary exists in packages/runner/src/supervisor/drain-table.ts (`WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE`, rank 20, terminalTarget RELEASED, with the design-765 note that "only an unchanged strongest WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE result makes the run resumable"), but no daemon path records it durably for an attempt.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND MUST BE COMPOSED, NOT REBUILT: a work-claim lifecycle with RELEASED already exists — `work-claim-read-model.ts:15` (`status: "OPEN" | "RELEASED"`), `work-lifecycle.ts:33-35` (`authority: "CLAIM_RELEASED"`, `successorState: "RELEASED"`), and `CONTEXT_LEGAL_STATES` including ACTIVE/SUSPECT/DRAINING/RELEASED. That is the CLAIM's release. What is missing is the attempt-level release disposition bundled with the lease and provider-slot state.

Deliverable: a durable record, written on the production release path, carrying the attempt's release disposition (reason, resumable, strongestReason, terminalTarget), its `attemptState`, and the lease and provider-slot refs with their states. Facts only — this task creates no hold, no PlanningRun, and grants no authority.

NOT in scope: terminal effect/resource enumeration (its own producer task), safe-boundary observation (its own producer task), the evidence reader itself (task-e62e3828), scheduler admission, or approval.

Owned paths: one new module under apps/daemon/src/work/ plus its .js bridge and focused test.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code. Daemon gates are red at baseline from foreign slices; apply the path-attributed baseline over the owned paths.
definitionOfDone: The release disposition is written by the PRODUCTION release path, not by a fixture: `grep -rn "WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE" --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep -v fixtures` returns a producer where it returned zero.

The record carries `reason`, `disposition{resumable, strongestReason, terminalTarget}`, `attemptState`, `leaseRef`, `leaseState`, `providerSlotRef` and `providerSlotState`, and a test reads every one back from durable bytes rather than from the writing call's return value.

The drain reason is taken from the production vocabulary in packages/runner/src/supervisor/drain-table.ts through the package root — never a locally retyped string — and a test asserts an unrecognised reason is refused with an exact code and layer rather than recorded.

A release that is NOT an unchanged strongest `WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE` records its true reason and does NOT present as resumable; a test drives at least one other drain reason and asserts the disposition differs, so the resumable path cannot be reached by default.

Lease and provider-slot states are read from their own durable authority, not asserted by the caller: a test supplies a caller-claimed state that contradicts the durable one and asserts the durable value wins, pinning the exact code and layer of whichever layer refused.
A mutation that hardcodes `terminalTarget: "RELEASED"` or `resumable: true` turns a NAMED test red.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` run with exit codes captured separately, the test leg prints a nonzero count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta over the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: No caller-supplied release state, drain reason, lease state or slot state may become authority. A caller may identify WHICH attempt; it may never supply WHAT happened to it.

Compose the existing work-claim lifecycle (work-lifecycle.ts, work-claim-read-model.ts) rather than rebuilding a second release concept. If it cannot express attempt-level release, say so explicitly rather than forking it.

Take the drain vocabulary from `@moe/runner`'s package root; do not retype `WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE` or the terminal targets locally, or the two definitions will drift and core's predicate will start refusing silently.
Fail closed: an unreadable lease, slot or disposition stays UNKNOWN and never becomes a recorded release. Real SqliteEventStore in tests, closed in a `finally` on every exit path.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source; commit only owned paths by explicit pathspec.

implementationPlan.description: TDD, vocabulary and refusal arms. Create `apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.test.ts` RED against the not-yet-written module. Pin the frozen vocabulary by hand — a closed code list plus one layer constant `DAEMON_ATTEMPT_RELEASE`, disjoint from the existing `DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT` — and assert every code is distinct. Refusal arms, each pinning the EXACT code AND layer and asserting NO durable row was written (read the store back; a handler that wrote then refused sails through a return-value assertion): (a) a disposition whose shape `parseDrainDisposition` rejects; (b) a shape-valid disposition that `isMonotonicDisposition` rejects because its `strongestReason` is not the highest-ranked member of its own `reasons` set; (c) one whose `terminalTarget` disagrees with its `strongestReason` — a SEPARATE case from (b), because the two halves fail for opposite reasons and a single code would leave a reviewer unable to tell a retargeted boundary from a downgraded reason set; (d) an unrecognised drain reason not in `DRAIN_REASONS`. Case (d) must use a string that is genuinely absent from the frozen list; assert the list does not contain it, so the case cannot go vacuous if the vocabulary grows.
implementationPlan.note:
Created apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.test.ts RED against the not-yet-written module. Confirmed RED: `npx vitest run --root . --config apps/daemon/package.json apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.test.ts` -> EXIT=1, "Cannot find module './attempt-release-disposition.js'".

Vocabulary pinned BY HAND (12 codes, asserted distinct and asserted as an exact sorted list) plus the layer constant DAEMON_ATTEMPT_RELEASE, explicitly asserted != DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT.

Refusal arms, each asserting exact code AND layer AND that NO durable row exists afterwards (read back through the module's own reader, so a write-then-refuse cannot hide behind the return value):
(a) shape rejected by parseDrainDisposition -> ATTEMPT_RELEASE_DISPOSITION_MALFORMED
(b) reason-set downgraded (URGENT_REVOKE rank 70 present while strongestReason claims WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE rank 20, target left at the CLAIMED reason's own target so only the rank half is wrong) -> ATTEMPT_RELEASE_DISPOSITION_DOWNGRADED
(c) retargeted (coherent reason set, ONLY terminalTarget wrong: SUCCEEDED against WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE) -> ATTEMPT_RELEASE_TARGET_MISMATCH, a SEPARATE code from (b)
(d) unrecognised reason "WORK_RELEASE_OR_RESUME" -> ATTEMPT_RELEASE_REASON_UNKNOWN, with `expect([...DRAIN_REASONS]).not.toContain(unknown)` FIRST so the case cannot go vacuous if the vocabulary grows.

Added one arm the plan did not list because it is load-bearing rather than decorative: a RECOGNISED reason absent from the disposition's own `reasons` set -> ATTEMPT_RELEASE_REASON_NOT_UNIONED. Without it a caller could record reason: "SUBMISSION_FINALIZE" beside a WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE strongest and the row's two reason fields would describe two different releases while core's predicate still admitted it.

Also added a positive control for the (b)/(c) discriminator: it works by asking whether ANY member of DRAIN_TERMINAL_TARGETS makes the disposition monotonic under the runner's own isMonotonicDisposition, so the test pins DRAIN_TERMINAL_TARGETS.length > 1 — if that vocabulary ever shrank to one member the two codes would silently collapse into one.

Fixtures are production-driven: seedReadyProject + runEffectActivateCommand commit a real activation into a real SqliteEventStore, and the ActivationLedgerRecord is read BACK via readFoundationActivationHistory, never kept from the command result. Stores are closed by the shared `afterEach(cleanupRestoreHarnesses)`.

implementationPlan.description: TDD, durable behaviour, same test file. (e) HAPPY PATH: an unchanged strongest `WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE` disposition is recorded and every field is read back FROM DURABLE BYTES via the module's own reader, never from the writing call's return value — `reason`, `resumable`, `strongestReason`, `terminalTarget`, `attemptState`, `leaseRef`, `leaseState`, `providerSlotRef`, `providerSlotState`. (f) NON-RESUMABLE PATH, which DoD 4 makes load-bearing: drive at least one OTHER member of `DRAIN_REASONS` and assert the recorded disposition DIFFERS and does not present as resumable — so the resumable path cannot be reached by default. Assert the two reasons used are actually different members. (g) CALLER CONTRADICTION, DoD 5: pass a caller-claimed `leaseState`/`providerSlotState` that contradicts the committed activation record and assert the DURABLE value is what lands, pinning the exact code and layer of whichever layer refused. (h) ABSENT vs AMBIGUOUS: zero rows and two rows on the attempt aggregate return DISTINCT codes — they demand opposite repairs. (i) UNREADABLE: tamper the stored bytes so the re-encode byte-compare fails, and assert a third, distinct code. Use a file-backed SQLite store and close it in `afterEach`; a held handle kills the vitest worker.
implementationPlan.note:
Appended the durable-behaviour cases to apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.test.ts. Still RED for the same reason (module absent) — re-verified after the append in step 5's first run.

(e) HAPPY PATH: every assertion is against `readAttemptRelease`'s answer, never against `written`. Asserts reason, disposition{resumable, strongestReason, terminalTarget}, attemptState, leaseRef, leaseState, providerSlotRef, providerSlotState, plus recordVersion / truthClass / attemptAggregateId. A `RELEASE_FIELDS.filter(f => !(f in row))` presence check guards against a field silently disappearing rather than merely changing value.

(f) NON-RESUMABLE: drives WORK_CANCEL -> CANCELLED, asserts the two reasons are genuinely different members of DRAIN_REASONS, asserts resumable false, and additionally asserts the whole disposition is NOT the resumable one — stated as a difference so the resumable path cannot be reached by default.

(g) CALLER CONTRADICTION: the caller record claims lease.state and providerSlot.state RELEASED while the committed activation says ACTIVE (both premises asserted first). The recorded row carries ACTIVE/ACTIVE. NO layer refuses here and the test says so explicitly — the claim is never consulted, so there is nothing to reject. The refusing half is covered by its own separate case: a caller record whose activationDigest contradicts the durable one is refused ATTEMPT_RELEASE_BINDING_MISMATCH at DAEMON_ATTEMPT_RELEASE with no row written.

(h) ABSENT vs AMBIGUOUS: same fixture asserts ABSENT before any write, then records one row, then plants a second event on the release aggregate and asserts AMBIGUOUS — two distinct codes.

(i) DRIFT: plants bytes '{"b":1,"a":2}' whose keys are out of canonical sort order, so they decode cleanly and fail the re-encode byte compare -> ATTEMPT_RELEASE_RECORD_DRIFT, a third distinct code.

Also added an ACTIVATION_UNREADABLE arm (a bound pointing at an aggregate carrying no activation).

Planted rows go through the store's own commitExpectedVersionDecision, so the reader's cardinality and byte-identity guards are reached by real committed evidence rather than a stub. Real file-backed SqliteEventStore throughout, closed by afterEach(cleanupRestoreHarnesses).

implementationPlan.description: Implement `apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.ts` plus the one-line bridge `attempt-release-disposition.js` (`export * from "./attempt-release-disposition.ts";`). Every sibling in this directory has one and it is git-tracked; without it the module is invisible at runtime while tsc and vitest both stay green. Exports: the frozen code vocabulary and `DAEMON_ATTEMPT_RELEASE` layer; `ATTEMPT_RELEASE_RECORD_VERSION`; `recordAttemptRelease(store, bound, record, dispositionValue)`; and `readAttemptRelease(store, attemptAggregateId)`. THE AUTHORITY RULE, and it is the whole point of the module: `dispositionValue` is validated through `parseDrainDisposition` then `isMonotonicDisposition` from the `@moe/runner` ROOT and is REFUSED rather than repaired — never re-derived locally, never retyped as a bare string union. The lease and provider-slot facts come from `record.lease.leaseId` / `record.lease.state` and `record.providerSlot`, RE-READ from the committed activation bytes (the same discipline `readStoredFoundationAttempt` uses: decode, re-encode, byte-compare), never from a caller argument. `resumable` is derived, not accepted: true only when the validated disposition's `strongestReason` is `WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE` and its `terminalTarget` is `RELEASED`. Commit ONE row on the attempt aggregate through the existing `commitFoundationPhase`-shaped expected-version port. Target <=250 physical lines; if the readers push it over, split them into `attempt-release-disposition-reads.ts` with its own `.js` bridge rather than growing past 400.

Implemented apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.ts (249 physical lines, under the 250 target) plus the one-line git-trackable bridge attempt-release-disposition.js (`export * from "./attempt-release-disposition.ts";`), matching every sibling in the directory.

The bridge guard suite apps/daemon/src/runtime-entrypoint.test.ts is EXIT=0, 4 passed, so the new .js bridge is accepted rather than merely present.

AUTHORITY RULE as implemented. The disposition is validated through parseDrainDisposition then isMonotonicDisposition, both imported from the @moe/runner ROOT, and REFUSED rather than repaired. Nothing local re-derives a rank or a terminal target and WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE is never retyped as a bare union.

How the two coherence codes stay separate WITHOUT re-deriving anything: isMonotonicDisposition folds "strongest reason is the highest-ranked member" and "terminal target matches that reason's target" into one boolean. coherenceRefusal asks the SAME predicate whether ANY member of DRAIN_TERMINAL_TARGETS would make the disposition monotonic. One would -> only the target is wrong (TARGET_MISMATCH). None would -> the reason set itself is downgraded (DOWNGRADED). drainRank and drainTargetOf stay unpublished and unused.

Lease/slot/attempt facts are RE-READ from the committed activation via readFoundationActivationHistory over store.readEvents(bound.aggregateId). The caller's ActivationLedgerRecord is consulted for IDENTITY ONLY (activationDigest, grantId, wrapperIdentity, intentId, attemptId) — states are deliberately excluded from that comparison, since a caller able to make its claimed lease state part of the agreement test could refuse the durable one.

resumable is DERIVED: true only when the VALIDATED disposition's strongestReason is WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE and its terminalTarget is RELEASED.

ONE deliberate deviation from the step text, and it is forced. The row is committed to a DEDICATED aggregate `attempt-release-<sha256>` derived from the attemptAggregateId (framed by ATTEMPT_RELEASE_RECORD_VERSION, exactly as deriveDispatchAggregateId frames itself), not onto bound.aggregateId. Writing onto the activation aggregate would BREAK the activation itself: readFoundationActivationHistory admits at most TRANSITION_ORDER.length + 1 events and requires the tail to be exactly GRANT_CONSUMED -> PREFLIGHT_REGISTERED -> PROCESS_OBSERVED, so a release event there returns FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED and durableActivation in foundation-attempt-service.ts starts refusing. The dedicated aggregate also keeps expectedVersion at 0 so ABSENT and AMBIGUOUS stay clean. The commit still goes through the commitFoundationPhase-shaped store.commitExpectedVersionDecision port with the event id COPIED from the grant (`<grantId>:RELEASED`), so a second release on the same activation collides on store-wide event-id uniqueness.

12 stable codes, all reachable, each a different repair. The writer answers from readAttemptRelease (re-decoded bytes that still re-encode byte-for-byte), never from the value it just wrote.

implementationPlan.note:
Consumer edge landed in apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-service.ts. Both settle call sites now route through one closure, `noteRelease(bound, record, settled)`, which picks the disposition from what the settle ACTUALLY answered rather than from which branch called it: `capture()` at the recordProvenFoundationAttempt site and `unproven()` at the settleFoundationAttempt site. File is 242 lines, under the 250 target (was 213).

Why the outcome and not the branch: recordProvenFoundationAttempt can itself answer an advisory UNKNOWN from the capture path, so `settled.ok` is the honest discriminator. SETTLE_DISPOSITIONS.PROVEN proposes WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE/RELEASED; SETTLE_DISPOSITIONS.UNPROVEN proposes WORK_CANCEL/CANCELLED. Both are only PROPOSED — recordAttemptRelease validates each through @moe/runner's own parseDrainDisposition + isMonotonicDisposition and refuses rather than repairs, so a mistyped literal here cannot land.

The release row's own refusal is deliberately NOT folded into the dispatch outcome, and the comment says so: this row is facts only, grants no authority, and a release fact that cannot be written must not change what the dispatch answers.

`grep -rn "WORK_RELEASE_OR_PAUSE" --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep -v fixtures` now returns six lines across attempt-release-disposition.ts (:15,:21,:154,:158) and foundation-attempt-service.ts (:100,:106). The two load-bearing ones are attempt-release-disposition.ts:158 (the resumable derivation) and foundation-attempt-service.ts:106 (the production proposal).

COMPOSITION PROVEN BY BEHAVIOUR, not only by grep. Added one case (12 lines) to the service's own suite apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-service.test.ts, inside the existing "reports the real runner's own UNSUPPORTED refusal on a non-Windows platform" case — the cheapest path that drives the WHOLE production dispatch end to end with the real launcher refusing at its own platform gate. It asserts the same dispatch also wrote the release row: reason WORK_CANCEL, disposition {resumable:false, strongestReason:"WORK_CANCEL", terminalTarget:"CANCELLED"}, and leaseState "ACTIVE" read from the durable activation. So the non-resumable path is what production actually reaches here, and the resumable path is unreachable by default.

planningNotes.risks:
1. CHAIN-LEVEL GAP THIS TASK CANNOT CLOSE, AND MUST NOT PRETEND TO. `LeaseRecord.state` is written ACTIVE at activation and the activation event is IMMUTABLE, and there is no lease-release or slot-release event anywhere in apps/daemon (grepped: the activation ledger writes `EffectActivationCommitted` plus exactly three transitions GRANT_CONSUMED / PREFLIGHT_REGISTERED / PROCESS_OBSERVED, and nothing else). So this producer will honestly record `leaseState: "ACTIVE"` and can never yield RELEASED until a lease-release producer lands. That is CORRECT and fail-closed for THIS task - its DoD asks only that the durable value wins over a caller claim - but it means the downstream reader task-e62e3828 still cannot assemble a valid ExpansionReleaseEvidence, whose `safeRelease` predicate demands leaseState === "RELEASED". A fifth prerequisite (durable lease and provider-slot release) is unowned on the board. DO NOT let a worker close this gap by defaulting leaseState to RELEASED; that is the exact caller-supplied authority the epic forbids.
2. The two `index-surface.test.ts` guards are hand-transcribed on purpose and live nowhere near the code being changed. Update BOTH axes - the count literal and the sorted name list. A worker who updates only the count gets a sorted-array diff failure that reads like an unrelated regression.
3. `expectTypeOf` is a NO-OP in the runner suite: its test script is `vitest run --root ../.. packages/runner/src` with no `--typecheck`. To pin a type-level fact so it actually fails, use a conditional-type assignment, which IS enforced because packages/runner/tsconfig.json includes src/**/*.ts.
4. Mutation drills run in a SHARED worktree. Snapshot file hashes and restore by content; `git checkout` as a drill restore destroys uncommitted work, and a peer's completion hook can commit a whole tree so `git status` reads clean while the drill is gone.
5. A file-backed SQLite handle left open kills the vitest worker outright - close before reopen, and close in `afterEach`.
6. Do not fold ABSENT into AMBIGUOUS or into DRIFT. Zero rows, two rows and unreadable bytes lead a reviewer to three different repairs; the sibling `readStoredFoundationAttempt` already keeps them separate and this module must match.
7. foundation-attempt-service.ts is at 213 of a 250-line target. An enthusiastic call-site edit pushes it over and turns a clean task into a forced split.
